x_route.disclosure.en: X route: the X counts, and the attention scores built from X posts, come from the 2026-10-07 research pass, whose notes name "x_search" reports and "X syndication" readbacks. Whether those are X's published interfaces, and whether a paid call was made, is not on record. An X count is a number of posts in our sample, never reach; no X post text, post link or figure is shown (a project's own X profile link stays).

method.scrub_effect.en: On the 2026-10-16 data, removing handles and X, LinkedIn, YouTube and Telegram content from the research dossier changed 30-day topic voices by -0.2% (29 of 157 topics; 13 project topics gained one voice when their X posts were placed on them), weight by -3.5% and signal by 1.7 points on average on 133 topics; 7-day voices and weight did not change. The effect ends when the dossier's posts, dated up to 2026-10-07, leave the 30-day window (about 2026-11-06).

dossier.x_figure_placeholder.en: An X figure is not shown here: X appears as counts only. See the method page.

state.proposed.en: proposed by the pipeline, not reviewed

cite.account_post.en: a post whose link names its account

figure.x_post.en: figure from an X post, not shown

figure.net_post.en: figure from a {net} post, not shown

source.posts_fetched_no_data.en: {n} posts fetched; no data this run for r/{subs}

source.dossier.en: {n} sampled posts, content cutoff {date} (static, refreshed by hand)

source.offline_not_fetched.en: not fetched in this offline rebuild

gauge.reason.tracker_not_read.en: insufficient data: the tracker (papers + repos) was not read in this run

gauge.reason.tracker_old.en: insufficient data: the tracker data is older than the 24h window

gauge.reason.no_top10.en: insufficient data: no covered news story had a post in the last 24h

gauge.reason.no_conversation.en: insufficient data: no conversation network was fetched

gauge.reason.no_rising.en: insufficient data: no topic had 4+ conversation posts in 7 days and 2+ in the last day

panel.risk.form.en: dated, sourced event log; no dial

coverage.feeds.en: Sampled feeds, not internet-wide totals: HN stories above 20 points, the Lobsters AI tag, nine Mastodon hashtags on mastodon.social, ten AI subreddits via the arctic-shift public archive (up to 1,000 newest posts per subreddit per run, so busy subreddits reach back about a week), twelve public AI newsletter feeds (the digest end point), lab and vendor announcement feeds (the Official network: where launches originate), tracker papers and repos, and the static HYPE research dossier. Bluesky appears only when an app password is configured. X appears only through the static dossier; it is not collected live.

coverage.topics.en: Topics come from a reviewable lexicon (topics_lexicon.json), automatic model-version names, and capitalised phrases used by at least three distinct authors (marked emerging).

coverage.counts.en: A node is only as strong as the posts behind it; posts from counts-only networks are counted, not shown.

projects.note.en: projects: live sampled feeds only (no tracker, no dossier); voices = distinct (network, author) pairs, nets = distinct networks; 0 means no matching post in our sampled feeds, not zero attention

organic.burst.high.en: {pct}% of {n} posts fell in the busiest 6 hours (from {at}Z). High: a synchronized push looks like this, but so does a launch or a news day.

organic.burst.spread.en: {pct}% of {n} posts fell in the busiest 6 hours (from {at}Z). Spread over time, as ongoing discussion usually is.

organic.burst.some.en: {pct}% of {n} posts fell in the busiest 6 hours (from {at}Z). Some clustering, typical of a news day.

organic.dupe.high.en: {pct}% of {n} comparable posts near-duplicate a post by a different author. High: copy-paste campaigns look like this; so do many people submitting the same article title.

organic.dupe.low.en: {pct}% of {n} comparable posts near-duplicate a post by a different author. Low: little copy-paste across authors.

organic.dupe.too_few.en: Too few posts of five or more words to compare ({n}).

organic.single.high.en: {pct}% of {n} authors with two or more stored posts posted only about this topic. High: new or single-purpose accounts look like this.

organic.single.low.en: {pct}% of {n} authors with two or more stored posts posted only about this topic. Most of them also post about other things.

organic.single.too_few.en: Too few authors with two or more stored posts to judge ({n}); one-post authors are not counted.

organic.link.high.en: {pct}% of {n} posts with a known target link point at the same URL. High: one link pushed by many accounts looks like this.

organic.link.varied.en: {pct}% of {n} posts with a known target link point at the same URL. Links are varied.

organic.link.unknown.en: Unknown: target links are kept only from {since} ({n} posts with one so far).

organic.repos.none.en: No tracked repo matches this topic.

organic.repos.farm_base.en: {n} tracked repos ranked in 30d match: {sa} stars>activity, {solo} solo, {spike} spike (stars>activity across all 30d rows: {base}%). Star growth without matching activity in most of them is a star-farming pattern.

organic.repos.backed_base.en: {n} tracked repos ranked in 30d match: {sa} stars>activity, {solo} solo, {spike} spike (stars>activity across all 30d rows: {base}%). Mostly backed by activity.

organic.repos.farm.en: {n} tracked repos ranked in 30d match: {sa} stars>activity, {solo} solo, {spike} spike. Star growth without matching activity in most of them is a star-farming pattern.

organic.repos.backed.en: {n} tracked repos ranked in 30d match: {sa} stars>activity, {solo} solo, {spike} spike. Mostly backed by activity.

organic.dossier.none.en: No HYPE research project maps to this topic.

index.scope.en: Ten AI stories from the last 24 hours, with their evidence and where each spread: attention in our sample, not a verdict on truth.

brief.out.sub.en: and {r} repos since {date}: output volume, not capability.

brief.hvs.sub.en: Substance: an official post or the story's own repo or paper link, shown beside the spread and never divided by it.

brief.hvs.unknown.en: {n} not known: official feeds not fully fetched.

brief.hvs.unknown.one.en: {n} not known: official feeds not fully fetched.

brief.hvs.mini.en: Voices per Top 10 story, by rank

brief.mv.sub.en: Last day's posts against the topic's 7-day daily average.

brief.top.rule.en: New today first, then by heat, from covered news stories with a post in the window. The rule and its tie break:

stale.since.en: Stale since {date}: missed the 06:00 BRT update of {deadline}

stale.note.en: No briefing has been published since the one for {date} (São Paulo date), and the next day's 06:00 deadline has passed. Everything below is as of {at}.

stale.failed.note.en: The refresh could not build a new briefing, so no value of the {date} briefing is carried over: the Top 10 and the gauges stay empty until a run succeeds.

stale.reason.pulse_failed.en: the Pulse step failed in refresh run {run}

ui.sem.title.en: Off until you select it. Search by meaning ranks rows with a small embedding model that runs in your browser: selecting it downloads about 28 MB from jsDelivr and Hugging Face once, then it is cached, and your query never leaves the browser. Without it every word of the query must match.

method.scope.en: How we count, rank and label, and the policy for verdicts, replies, corrections and removals. The page renders the files as written; formulas and code are the same in both languages.

audit.scope.en: What anyone can check about each daily briefing: the method version and config hash it was built with, and the record that fixes it in time. Records not yet published read so.

audit.today.sub.en: The values every evidence record of briefing.json carries.

audit.hash.note.en: The config hash covers the method version, the method text and {files}.

audit.ledger.sub.en: One entry per published briefing: its date, the SHA256 the ledger records for its manifest beside the SHA256 of the asset on its dated Release, and the state of its timestamp proof.

audit.ledger.none.en: No ledger entry yet: the first is written by the first scheduled run whose deploy passes the per-deploy checks.

audit.attest.how.en: Each day's manifest is attested in its own job after the refresh. Check the latest ({date}) after downloading it from its Release:

audit.ots.how.en: The proof of the {date} manifest, beside the manifest itself on its dated Release:

audit.ots.pending.en: This proof is still pending: the calendars have not yet put it in a Bitcoin block, so ots verify cannot accept it yet. A later refresh upgrades it in place and records its block in that run's own ledger entry.

audit.ots.node.en: With your own Bitcoin node, download both files and run the OpenTimestamps client; it checks the block header against your node:

audit.ots.explorer.en: Without a node, as the refresh does: the pinned client opentimestamps 0.4.9 takes the block header from the public Esplora explorer at https://blockstream.info/api and assumes that explorer's block is valid.

audit.attest.sub.en: A Sigstore attestation of each day's manifest, which gh attestation verify checks.

audit.ots.sub.en: An OpenTimestamps proof of each day's manifest: pending until a ledger entry records its Bitcoin block, then anchored.

audit.owner.sub.en: Verdicts, corrections and removal requests change only by a merged pull request.

brief.hvs.none.en: of {n} not known: official feeds not fetched

fold.window.en: This link comes from the old console: its {from} window is not kept here, so this page shows {to}.

fold.filters.en: This link comes from the old console: its search filters (counts, comparisons, dates) are no longer supported, so the words are matched as text.

soai.line.en: today only · {days} of 14 ledger days · no combined score

status.scope.en: What dehype reads today, what is ready or waiting to be connected, and what comes next. Live statuses are read from the latest run's data files; the other rows come from an owner-reviewed plan.

status.audit.more.en: Details and commands on the Audit page

status.sources.sub.en: One row per source. Live rows carry the status and detail the latest run recorded; the other groups come from the owner-reviewed plan.

status.group.live.sub.en: Read by the daily refresh. A source named in more than one data file is shown once, with the file it was read from.

status.group.ready.sub.en: The key or token is stored; the collector is not written yet.

status.group.pending.sub.en: Applied for; waiting on the provider.

status.group.held.sub.en: Not collected: paid, or held until a condition is met.

status.group.free.sub.en: No paid key needed; the collector is not written yet.

status.roadmap.sub.en: What each step delivers, in order. Every step after S1 is its own wish.

status.unread.en: {file} could not be read, so its sources are not listed.

ui.foot.counts.en: Counts are posts in our sample, not internet-wide totals.

ui.error.en: Could not load this page's data:

ui.path.en: Path: first post per network, oldest first

stories.scope.en: Every story our sampled feeds saw in the last 7 days, each with its evidence record: how many voices, on which networks, and what is still unchecked. It measures attention in our sample; it does not say whether a story is true.

stories.k.news_sub.en: covered stories; the rest is chatter

stories.map.sub.en: Each dot is a story at its first post; height is voices (square-root scale). Select a dot to open its record.

output.scope.en: Papers published and repositories created in the window, by research area, among the items our tracker ranked. It counts output in our tracker; it does not measure the field's total output or the quality of any item.

output.k.tracked_sub.en: {p} papers and {r} repos tracked in all

output.chart.title.en: Papers and repos by area, last {n} days

output.chart.sub.en: Each panel on its own scale, areas in the same order. Select an area to list its items below.

output.gauge.same.en: Same counts as the briefing gauge "{name}".

output.gauge.differs.en: These counts differ from the briefing gauge "{name}": the tracker file is newer than the briefing.

output.gauge.other.en: The briefing gauge "{name}" reads the 7-day window.

output.table.caption.en: {area}, ranked by the tracker's {wk} score where it has one

hype.scope.en: A research dossier on AI projects: sampled attention next to evidence of substance. It shows where attention and evidence part ways in our sample; it does not validate any project or measure its real use.

hype.cut.en: Research dossier, content cut {date}, not in the daily refresh

hype.verdict.note.en: The gap class is a heuristic and never fills this slot; verdicts are the owner's, on claims and stories, in verdicts.json.

hype.earliest.en: earliest post in the sample on {net}, not a proven origin

hype.skeptic.note.en: sampled criticism, not checked against a primary source

dossier.pt_notice.en: Dossier text in English; the Portuguese version awaits review

ui.generated.en: Generated {at}. "New today" means the story's first post in our sample came in the 24 hours before then.

hype.k.ahead_sub.en: gap class, heuristic only, not validation ({n} with any positive gap, most with insufficient coverage)

panel.jobs.context_note.en: context, not a forecast: general labour figures and hiring posts; none of them attributes a change to AI

ind.hn.name.en: Hacker News "Who is hiring?" posts that mention AI

ind.bls.notice.en: BLS.gov cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from BLS.gov.

ind.hn.counted.en: top-level posts with text (deleted posts left out); a month still open counts the posts so far

ind.bls.CES6054150001.en: Computer systems design and related services

ind.bls.CES5051800001.en: Computing infrastructure, data processing and web hosting

ind.reason.not_fetched.en: insufficient data: not fetched in this run

ind.reason.failed.en: insufficient data: the source failed in this run ({error})

ind.reason.no_series.en: insufficient data: no listed series was in the response

ind.reason.no_thread.en: insufficient data: no hiring thread had a post

ind.reason.no_project.en: insufficient data: no project had every article and day

ind.reason.series_missing.en: insufficient data: the series was not in the response

ind.reason.wiki_incomplete.en: insufficient data: {n} of {total} articles had all {days} days in the response

ind.reason.no_article.en: insufficient data: no article was read

brief.jobs.scope.en: for any change in jobs attributed to AI

brief.wiki.note.en: user views of a fixed list of articles: attention to these pages, not awareness

status.ind.sub.en: Wired into the briefing's Jobs and page-view panels, with no key. Each one's terms were read before it was used, on the date shown.

status.ind.terms.bls.en: US government data in the public domain (BLS asks to be cited as the source). The API terms ask users to cite the date the data were accessed or retrieved and require the statement “BLS.gov cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from BLS.gov.”; both are shown with the panel. Public API v1, no key: 25 queries a day and 25 series a query; we make one query a day.

status.ind.terms.hn_hiring.en: Y Combinator publishes the Hacker News data through its public API and states no licence; its terms of use bar scraping the site itself, and the Algolia search API page states no terms we could read. The route the tracker already reads. Counts only: no post text or poster name is stored or shown.

status.ind.terms.wikipedia.en: Data under CC0 1.0 (Wikimedia Analytics API access policy). The requests carry a descriptive User-Agent with a contact and are made one after another, as the policy asks.
